recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

reckY5kIUk9PGpkPK.Bio: Homie Romie hosts the "Rising From The Ashes" podcast, researching alternative history and esoteric topics such as ancient royal regalia and theories connecting them to consciousness technology.
reckY5kIUk9PGpkPK.Name: Homie Romie

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Money as an Alchemical Working", "body": "Chance opened by arguing that there was no economics without alchemy and no money without the occult, and he built the evening around Tracy Twyman's book Money Grows on the Tree of Knowledge. Homie Romie said the book traced how Western money tied back to alchemical practice and to magical workers such as Bacon, and he connected that to banks shutting down that week. The conversation also noted that Twyman wrote a second money book, Solomon's Treasure, and Mario said he owned an original copy."}, {"title": "Serpents, Shekels, and the Dollar Sign", "body": "Chance showed a Tyre shekel bearing two pillars and a serpent wrapped around a tree, which he said looked like a dollar sign, and he linked it to the brazen serpent of the Hebrew scriptures. He argued that the Hebrew words for serpent and Messiah shared a gematria value of 358, and he suggested money was therefore cast as a cure and a savior. Mario argued that the central pole in Freemasonic art represented the world axis and the pole star, and that the saying money makes the world go round referred to it."}, {"title": "Cain, Coinage, and Temple Wheat", "body": "Chance argued that Cain, coin and corn were linked by language, and he suggested money was a confidence game run by an ancient maritime priest class. Homie Romie read from Twyman's book that coinage began around 3000 BC in the temples of Ishtar, where a bushel of wheat bought a coin and the coin bought a visit with a priestess. Romie added that he saw modern workers selling themselves for money in a similar way. Mario said Freemasons may call each other brothers in reference to Cain and Abel."}, {"title": "Templars, Cipher Notes, and Tithes", "body": "Chance recounted the lore that the Knights Templar found something beneath Jerusalem and then built what amounted to a banking system, with depositors receiving coded notes redeemable at another castle. Romie shared slides describing the order as warrior monks who moved money safely, and Chance asked whether Philip the Fair destroyed them for their wealth. Chance also argued that the tithe, a tenth passed up a chain of districts, belonged to an ecclesiastical system older than Christianity."}, {"title": "Gold, Fiat Money, and Time", "body": "Chance described the 1933 order requiring gold to be surrendered to Federal Reserve banks and argued that the gold standard had been replaced with a time standard that attaches self-worth to hours worked. He read Twyman's claim that fractional reserve lending ties the money supply to velocity, and that the modern economy compels even useless work so the transformation of paper into gold feels real. Chance concluded that a person's time is their real spiritual currency."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Homie Romie of Rising From the Ashes Podcast joins us tonight to discuss the alchemy of economics. How exactly do the financial wizards convert the dross of debt into the extraction of gold? We will explore the roots of banking in the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
